text:
alex_support: Hey team — incoming from ACME. They invited an external contractor (contractor@acme-external.com) to a project yesterday, gave them Project Viewer role via the Console invite flow, but the contractor reports a 403 when opening the project console and when trying to fetch project metadata via the API. Customer says the invite shows as accepted. Can someone triage? :thinking_face:

idp-sync-bot: SCIM push received for user contractor@acme-external.com -> created user id u_8f3c, groups: [acme:contractors]. Mapping rule applied: external_collab -> role none. (event id e-9923)

alex_support: Repro steps from customer (copied):
1) Invite contractor@acme-external.com from Org -> Members -> Invite (Project Viewer, project: acme-prod)
2) Contractor accepts invite via email link, gets redirected to console and can see org/project list
3) Clicking into acme-prod -> "Project settings" or "Billing" shows 403 page (permission denied)
4) They also tried API: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/projects/acme-prod` returns 403 with body `\{"error":"forbidden","reason":"insufficient_project_permissions"\}`

maya_idp: Thanks, adding context — ACME uses Okta with SCIM group push + SSO enforcement. Two likely possibilities: (A) user is created as a "guest"/external identity that doesn't pick up org->project role inheritance, or (B) group -> role mapping in SCIM hasn't pushed the acme:contractors group to map to the Project Viewer role. Quick checks: confirm `role_source` and `group_memberships` in our user record, and whether the SCIM push included the `roles` claim.

sre_lee: Can you paste the repro curl that fails? Also share the auth token kind — looks like they used a console-created API key? If the token is a user personal API key, the policy engine should evaluate project roles.

alex_support: Here's the raw curl snippet customer provided (redacted):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED" \n  https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/projects/acme-prod

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
\{"error":"forbidden","reason":"insufficient_project_permissions","details":\{"user_id":"u_8f3c","role_source":"invite"\}\}
```

maya_idp: That `role_source: "invite"` is the suspicious bit. If a user accepted an invite but the org enforces SSO with SCIM group sync, sometimes we create the account first (invite flow) and later SCIM pushes groups, but the role assignment code expects `role_source` to be `scim` or `group`. There's a known corner case where `invite` entries don't get merged into group inheritance if the `primary_email` domain doesn't match the org's verified domain and the system marks them as external.

julian_platform: Filing notes: looks like a two-part remediation — immediate customer workaround + long-term fix. Immediate: org admin can manually add the user to the project role from Org -> Members -> Manage membership -> add role on project (this bypasses group mapping). Also re-invite using their SSO-backed email (if they have a corp identity) or update SCIM to include the external domain in allowed group push.

sre_lee: For internal triage I ran a quick lookup on u_8f3c in prod audit logs. Relevant snippets:
```
[2026-03-12T08:14:05Z] user.create id=u_8f3c source=invite email=contractor@acme-external.com
[2026-03-12T08:17:12Z] scim.push user=contractor@acme-external.com groups=[acme:contractors] event=e-9923
[2026-03-12T08:17:12Z] group.map acme:contractors -> role=project_viewer target=acme-prod result=applied
[2026-03-12T08:17:14Z] role.assign user=u_8f3c role_source=scim role=project_viewer target=acme-prod
[2026-03-12T08:17:15Z] policy.eval user=u_8f3c role_sources=[invite] decision=deny
```
So it looks like the group mapping and assignment did run, but policy.eval still sees only `invite` in `role_sources`. That matches the corner case.

maya_idp: Exactly — root cause: race between invite-created identity and SCIM sync leads to inconsistent `role_sources` index. There's a small bug where `role.assign` for `scim` does not update the flattened `role_sources` cache used by the policy evaluator when `invite` is present. I've seen this before in ENG-PLATFORM-#4728.

alex_support: Customer asked for workaround they can try now. Can we give step-by-step for on-call or the customer?

julian_platform: Workarounds (ranked):
1) Org admin manual grant (fastest): Org -> Members -> find contractor -> Edit membership -> Add Project Viewer for acme-prod. Confirm they can access console immediately.
2) Force SCIM re-sync from IdP side (push groups again) and then nudge internal indexer to rehydrate role_sources: run internal admin job `POST /internal/admin/users/u_8f3c/refresh_roles` (requires internal creds). Example: `http --auth :$INTERNAL_TOKEN POST https://console.internal.redwood/api/admin/users/u_8f3c/refresh_roles`
3) Quick internal hotfix: run migration script that recalculates role_sources for users created within the last 24h in acme org: `scripts/reindex_role_sources --org acme --since 24h` (eng only).

sre_lee: I executed (2) for this user and re-ran the policy eval — contractor now has `role_sources=[invite, scim]` and the API call returns 200. Verified with the customer (they confirmed console access). :white_check_mark: 

idp-sync-bot: SCIM push processed for user contractor@acme-external.com (replay) -> group map applied -> role_sources updated.

maya_idp: Follow-ups:
- I'll open an engineering bug with reproducer and the log traces (ENG-PLATFORM-4728).
- Recommend we add a small defensive update in the role assign path to update the policy cache even when `invite` exists. This should make future SCIM pushes idempotent for invite-created accounts.

julian_platform: I'll add a short KB entry for Support with the manual grant steps + internal admin refresh command. KB gap noted.

alex_support: Thanks all — passing back to customer with steps: 1) Org admin can manually add project role OR ask us to trigger internal refresh, 2) if they prefer a permanent fix we'll track via ENG-PLATFORM-4728. Notifying ACME now. :phone: 

sre_lee: Marking thread resolved for now — please re-open if it recurs after SCIM pushes. :eyes:
